name: Junkboxes Needed
summary: Fahrad keeps Ravenholdt supplied with locked boxes for rogue training. He trades specialized throwing knives for authentic heavy junkboxes, and his demand never ends.

sections.title: Sharpening Ravenholdt's Talons
sections.body: Ravenholdt Manor hides in the mountains above Hillsbrad Foothills, where training never ceases. Master thief Fahrad oversees the guild's operatives and prizes skill at picking locks. Zan supplies practice contraptions for new recruits. Fahrad finds them too crude for experienced thieves who must open stubborn mechanisms in the field.

sections.title: A Curiously Open Arrangement
sections.body: Fahrad pays for heavy junkboxes stolen from dangerous targets across Azeroth, and accepts them in batches. Only skilled thieves can lift the boxes from their marks in the wild, but anyone may bring them to the manor. Even boxes stripped of major valuables earn his favor and finely balanced throwing knives from the manor. A token coin must remain inside, to motivate the initiates.

faq.q: Why does Fahrad want these junkboxes?
faq.answer: Ravenholdt's apprentice rogues need realistic locks to practice on. Zan, the manor's resident craftsman, makes practice chests that Fahrad considers too elementary for anyone past the beginner stage. So he requires real lockboxes taken from dangerous marks.

faq.q: Where does this task take place?
faq.answer: The exchange takes place at Ravenholdt Manor, a secret refuge for the thieves' guild in the mountains north of Hillsbrad Foothills.

faq.q: Can only rogues turn in this quest?
faq.answer: Anyone who brings heavy junkboxes to the manor may deliver them. Skilled thieves steal the boxes from their marks through pickpocketing.

faq.q: Why must there still be coins left inside the boxes?
faq.answer: Fahrad requires a few coins to remain in each chest, giving rogues in training a practical reason to practice their lockpicking.

faq.q: What does Ravenholdt offer in exchange?
faq.answer: Contributors earn guild standing and finely crafted throwing knives from Fahrad. He sardonicly hopes they find a place in someone's heart.

faq.q: Who is Zan that Fahrad complains about?
faq.answer: Zan supplies Ravenholdt with locks and practice mechanisms. Fahrad finds Zan's crude work fit only for the rawest beginners, not serious operatives.

angles.text: As a rogue, you can get these heavy chests by pickpocketing seasoned adversaries. Ravenholdt gives that illicit skill a place to serve.
Ravenholdt lies in contested Lordaeron territory and operates independently. As an Alliance wanderer, you can bring it contracts without regard for faction lines.
As a Horde operative, you can brave the trek into the Hillsbrad mountains. Ravenholdt is indifferent to faction loyalties and prizes useful illicit goods above all else.
